description: ClickHouse column-oriented OLAP database. Reads and writes over the async SQLAlchemy clickhouse+asynch transport (the clickhouse-sqlalchemy dialect on the asynch native-protocol driver): username/password authentication, a three-value ssl_mode (disable / require / verify-full) realized through the driver's secure/verify connect arguments, and schema/table/view discovery via ClickHouse's INFORMATION_SCHEMA views. ClickHouse's native protocol has no STARTTLS-style upgrade - TLS is a separate listener (9440) from the plaintext one (9000) - so ssl_mode and port must agree. Write-path facts are declared honestly rather than conveniently: ClickHouse has no MERGE, no ON CONFLICT and no ON DUPLICATE KEY, so merge_form is 'none' and upsert streams are refused at handshake instead of silently duplicating rows (row-collapsing upserts are a table-engine property - ReplacingMergeTree plus FINAL - not a statement grammar the engine can render); DDL is never transactional, so staging uses a real MergeTree table created and dropped outside any transaction. No first-class ADBC driver and no Arrow Flight SQL endpoint exist for ClickHouse, so the SQLAlchemy transport is the only supported path; batches land through the native columnar block insert the driver performs on executemany, which is why bulk_load declares no separate mechanism and why write_unit asks the coalescer for large batches (ClickHouse penalizes small, frequent inserts with part explosion).

ui.label: Host
ui.help_text: Hostname or IP address of the ClickHouse server. This connector speaks ClickHouse's native TCP protocol, not the HTTP interface, so give the host that serves the native listener.

ui.label: Port
ui.help_text: TCP port of the ClickHouse native protocol listener. ClickHouse serves plaintext on 9000 and TLS on 9440 as two separate listeners - there is no in-band upgrade - so this must agree with SSL Mode: 9440 for require/verify-full (the default), 9000 for disable.

ui.label: Database
ui.help_text: ClickHouse database to connect to. A ClickHouse database is the schema level - there is no catalog level above it - and 'default' is the database a stock server creates.

ui.label: Username
ui.help_text: ClickHouse user. 'default' is the user a stock server creates.

ui.label: Password
ui.help_text: Password for the ClickHouse user. A password is required: a stock server's passwordless 'default' user is not a supported configuration for this connector.

ui.label: SSL Mode
ui.help_text: How the native-protocol connection is secured. The driver exposes TLS as a 'secure' switch plus a 'verify' switch, and its only channel for a custom CA bundle is a filesystem path, which a stored secret cannot supply - so no CA certificate input is offered and verify-full validates against the host's system trust store. Because TLS lives on its own listener, changing this usually means changing the port too.

options.label: Disable - plaintext connection (native listener, usually port 9000)
Require - encrypted, but the server certificate is not verified
Verify Full - encrypted, certificate and host name verified against the system CA store (default)
